solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Having a feeling of foreboding now one starts to experience nasty tremors

parts.note: the present is the time now
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the starts of the next three words are taken, their opening letters only

explanation.surface: Someone senses trouble coming as unpleasant tremors begin to be felt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes the first letters of experience, nasty and tremors, giving ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Presentiment is an intuitive sense that something, usually bad, is about to happen; the adjective describes having that dread.

clue.text: Year after college involved in crazy caper to do with money

indicators.note: the year letter comes behind everything else
the college word is caught up within the jumbled letters
crazy signals the letters of caper going wild into a new order

parts.note: uni is the informal word for university, a college

explanation.surface: A student a year on from university gets mixed up in some wild money-making scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' makes PECAR, which 'involved in' opens up; 'after' puts the Y last, though the clue mentions it first.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecuniary is the formal adjective for matters relating to cash and finance.

clue.text: Former writer ultimately queries expensive outlay

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-partner
a pen is a writing tool

indicators.note: ultimately points at the final letter of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A one-time author raises doubts about some costly spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letters of queries and expensive, S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlay is money spent, a straightforward synonym for cost or spending.

clue.text: Ten operas rewritten in international language

indicators.note: rewritten suggests the letters of the two words are set down again in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Ten operas are translated into a language meant for the whole world.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is the best-known invented language, devised by Zamenhof for use between nations.

clue.text: Draw boundaries of ruins in rows

parts.note: a draw in sport is a tie

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its outside letters, first and last

explanation.surface: An instruction to sketch the edges of ruined buildings laid out in lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boundaries of' takes R and S, the outside letters of ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiers are rows set one above another, as in a stadium or a wedding cake.

clue.text: English value current and former profs

parts.note: merit is worth or value
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: Retired English professors are praised for their value, past and present.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus professors are retired ones who keep their title as an honour; this is the Latin plural.

clue.text: One being coached in statute examination

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A pupil is being prepared for a law exam on statutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters spanning statUTE Examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutee is a student who is being taught by a tutor.

clue.text: Summing up in chat about European Commission

indicators.note: about means the chat word goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: rap is old slang for a talk or chat

explanation.surface: A summary given in an informal talk about the European Commission.
explanation.definitionFit: A recap, short for recapitulation, is a summary restating the main points.

clue.text: Echo coming from beaver tangled with tree by river

indicators.note: by means set next to, so the river letter sits beside the jumble
tangled shows the letters of beaver and tree twisted together into a new order

explanation.surface: A sound comes from a beaver caught up in a tree near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangled' gives EVERBERATE from the two animal-and-plant words; 'by' sets R in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo is to resound or ring back, which is what a sound that reverberates does.

clue.text: Stopped deep river swirling round outlet

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around the outlet word
swirling shows the letters churned into a new order, like water

parts.note: a vent is an opening that lets air or gas out

explanation.surface: Water in a deep river eddying round a drain was halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' gives PREED, which goes 'round' the outlet; 'deep' reads as an adjective but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Prevented means kept from happening, blocked, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Mandate is rewritten to include Royal Marines laying down weapons

indicators.note: to include means the jumbled letters take the abbreviation inside them
rewritten suggests the words are drafted again with letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A redrafted mandate brings Royal Marines into a deal on arms reduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' turns MANDATE IS into DISAAMENT, which takes RM inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Disarmament is the giving up or reducing of military arms; laying down weapons is a phrase for it.

clue.text: After third of November intern trained as a wine-seller

indicators.note: after places the jumble behind the selected letter
the third letter of the next word is the one selected
trained suggests the letters being schooled into a new shape

explanation.surface: A trainee taken on in November learns to become a wine merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third of November' gives V; 'trained' turns INTERN into INTNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintner is a wine merchant, a dealer in wine.

clue.text: Small glittery fish with black eyes

definitions.meaning: small silvery freshwater minnows of North America go by this name
bruised eyes from a punch are informally called by this name

explanation.surface: Little shiny fish with dark eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a name for small silvery fish and slang for bruised black eyes, both things that shine.

clue.text: Pillage about half of street

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: half of takes the first three of the six letters

parts.note: an avenue is a street

explanation.surface: Looting spreads around half the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes AVE, the first half of AVENUE, a word for a street.
explanation.definitionFit: To reave is an archaic verb meaning to plunder or rob by force.

clue.text: One voids last of wagers from run with fillies going wild

indicators.note: going wild shows the letters running loose into a new order
from signals the selected letter is taken away from the horses word
last of takes the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone cancels bets after a race in which young mares ran wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of wagers' is S, taken 'from' FILLIES to leave FILLIE; that plus RUN is shuffled by 'going wild'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who voids something cancels or invalidates it, which is exactly what this agent noun means.

clue.text: Perhaps hen's crackle regularly provides teatime treat

parts.note: a hen is an example of a layer, a bird that lays eggs; the 's is a link

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A hen's clucking produces a sweet cake for afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the odd letters of crackle, C A K E.
explanation.definitionFit: A cake built from stacked sponge tiers with filling is a classic thing served at tea.

clue.text: I realised, unfortunately, I'm an impractical person

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters coming out badly, in a muddled order

explanation.surface: Someone sadly admits they are a dreamer with no practical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sees things as perfect rather than as they are is a dreamer, an unrealistic sort.

clue.text: Strangely gloomy yet it describes word derivation

indicators.note: strangely shows the letters arranged in an odd new order

explanation.surface: An oddly sombre thing explains where words come from.
explanation.definitionFit: Etymology is the study of word origins, the history of how words came about.

clue.text: Old British rhyme written on this side of coin?

parts.note: verse is rhyming poetry

explanation.surface: An old British poem is inscribed on a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this side' fits a coin's head side, the one facing you.
explanation.definitionFit: The obverse is the face of a coin bearing the main design, usually the head.

clue.text: Short article by Greek character? Yet another one!

indicators.note: short means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: the is the definite article
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A brief newspaper piece on a Greek personality prompts a weary groan.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'Greek character' just before it: the answer is a further Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is another letter of the Greek alphabet, following the eta in the wordplay.

clue.text: Wilson, for one, gets brown around this part of sailing vessel

indicators.note: around means the brown word wraps the abbreviation

parts.note: to toast is to brown under heat
Harold Wilson was a UK Prime Minister, abbreviated PM

explanation.surface: Harold Wilson gets a suntan on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A topmast is the section of mast above the lower mast on a sailing ship.

clue.text: Excessively attentive to a Latin paramour

parts.note: a paramour is a lover

explanation.surface: A Latin lover is overly affectionate.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all over someone is an idiom for fussing over them with too much attention.

clue.text: It follows fifty-one miles to reach border

indicators.note: follows puts the first word behind the other pieces

parts.note: LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Fifty-one miles of travel brings you to the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary or edge, the point beyond which something cannot go.

clue.text: Irritated as gun, though not loud, finally exploded

indicators.note: not means without, so the loud letter is dropped

parts.note: a rifle is a gun
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: finally points at the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Annoyed because a gun went off at last, even if quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing F from RIFLE leaves RILE; 'finally exploded' adds D.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled means annoyed or angered, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Hesitation when returning heart-throb gets rebuff

indicators.note: returning means the hesitation word is read backwards

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
a pulse is the throb of the heart

explanation.surface: A pin-up idol is turned down after some hesitation on coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart-throb' looks like a dreamboat; here it is the beat of the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse is to drive back or reject, as a rebuff does.

clue.text: Tragic heroine seen originally wearing green article

indicators.note: wearing puts the single letter inside the green word, as if dressed in it

parts.note: emerald is a shade of green

indicators.note: originally points at the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A doomed heroine is spotted dressed in green.
explanation.definitionFit: Esmeralda is the ill-fated gypsy girl in Victor Hugo's The Hunchback of Notre-Dame.

clue.text: A singular collection that's worth having

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a set is a collection of things

explanation.surface: One unique collection is valuable to own.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful or valuable thing, something one is glad to possess.

clue.text: Time restrictions initially stop me for instance becoming a fashion icon

indicators.note: initially points at the first letter of the preceding word

parts.note: an end is a stop or finish
the person writing the clue, speaking as me, is the crossword setter

explanation.surface: Time limits stop the setter becoming a style leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the puzzle's author, a setter: a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leads fashion, starting styles that others copy, is a style pioneer.
